question: For $$y=e^x(x\log x-1),\qquad x>0,$$ find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ and hence establish the relation $$\frac{dy}{dx}-y=e^x(1+\log x).$$
explanation:
Differentiation
Given $$y=e^x(x\log x-1).$$ Using the product rule, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=e^x(x\log x-1)+e^x\frac{d}{dx}(x\log x-1).$$ Now, $$\frac{d}{dx}(x\log x)=\log x+x\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)=\log x+1.$$ Therefore, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=e^x(x\log x-1)+e^x(\log x+1).$$ Simplifying, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=e^x\left(x\log x+\log x\right)=e^x(x+1)\log x.$$

Verification
Using $y=e^x(x\log x-1)$, $$\frac{dy}{dx}-y=e^x(x+1)\log x-e^x(x\log x-1).$$ Taking $e^x$ common, $$\frac{dy}{dx}-y=e^x\left[(x+1)\log x-x\log x+1\right].$$ Hence, $$\frac{dy}{dx}-y=e^x(\log x+1).$$

Final Result
Thus, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=e^x(x+1)\log x$$ and consequently $$\frac{dy}{dx}-y=e^x(1+\log x).$$
